artists.biography: Ride were a British shoegazing band that formed in 1988 in Oxford, England, consisting of Andy Bell, Mark Gardener, Laurence "Loz" Colbert, and Steve Queralt. The band were initially part of the "shoegazing" scene that emerged in England during the early 1990s. Following the break-up of the band in 1996, members moved on to various other projects, most notably Bell who became the bassist for Oasis. In 2001, the band members were briefly reunited for a one-off performance for a television show. Their debut album 'Nowhere' has been named one of the greatest albums of the shoegazing genre, Nowhere was voted number 74 on Pitchfork Media's list of the Top 100 Albums of the 1990s, and closing track "Vapour Trail" was voted at number 145 on Pitchfork's Top 200 Tracks of the 90s. The album is also included in the book '1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die'.

perplexity.description:
Tarantula, released in March 1996, is the fourth studio album by British rock band Ride. Marking a departure from their earlier shoegaze sound, the album embraces a more straightforward alternative rock style with elements of British traditional rock and indie influences. This shift reflects the band's evolution toward a rawer, more guitar-driven sound, moving away from the lush, atmospheric textures that characterized their critically acclaimed first two albums, Nowhere (1990) and Going Blank Again (1992).

The album holds a unique place in Ride's discography as it was released shortly after the band had split, making it their final studio album before their long hiatus. Commercially, Tarantula reached No. 21 on the UK Albums Chart, a notable drop compared to the top 5 positions of their previous records, indicating a more mixed reception. Critically, the album received a polarized response, with some critics and fans appreciating the band's attempt to evolve their sound, while others lamented the loss of the signature shoegaze elements that had defined their earlier work. Despite this, Tarantula remains an important document of Ride's late-90s phase and their exploration of rock beyond their shoegaze roots.
